opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kenneth Burch (employee ID E007) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E007.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kenneth Burch (E007) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write (admin would require the Payroll Specialist role, which the Analyst role does not own). Requested level is at the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows Kenneth Burch (E007) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, maximum is read. Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Kenneth Burch (E007) is a full-time Analyst per the HR record. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, which the Analyst role does not own, so the maximum for this full-time employee is write (admin requires role ownership). The requested level (write) is at the maximum and not above it, so write is granted. Note: the Security note lists the employee as a contractor, which conflicts with HR; I rely on HR as the authoritative source for employment type, and under the full-time policy the requested write is permissible.

But wait — if security record is correct that they're a contractor, then max would be read (basic training).
